findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns "Clients" instead of client IDs and misses per-client resources
findings.body:
`getClientsWithPermission` iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` and adds `resource.getName()`.

Per-client resources created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never get a type. They are made with `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner)` and no `setType`. Only the all-clients resource from `init()` has type `Clients`.

As a result:
- Individual client permissions are never found.
- When the all-clients permission is granted, the returned set contains the literal string "Clients" rather than any client id.

Any caller that treats the result as a set of client IDs gets wrong data. Either nothing is found, or a bogus id is returned.

findings.title: canView(client) short-circuits on all-clients VIEW, so per-client deny permissions cannot restrict view
findings.body:
`canView(ClientModel)` returns true as soon as `canView()` is true. `canView()` includes `hasPermission(VIEW)`, which evaluates only the all-clients "Clients" resource.

So if an admin is granted VIEW on all clients, a per-client NEGATIVE VIEW permission for a specific client is never consulted. The admin can still view that client.

This contradicts the resource-specific-overrides-type semantics used elsewhere in V2. For users, `testViewUserPermission` shows a per-user deny overriding the all-users allow. Here an administrator cannot hide individual clients from someone holding all-clients VIEW.

`canView(client)` should only short-circuit on the admin roles (`canViewClientDefault`). The VIEW decision should go through `hasPermission(client, VIEW)`, which already falls back to the all-clients resource.

findings.title: NPE when the "Clients" type resource is absent
findings.body:
When no per-client resource exists, the code loads the type resource via `getResourceTypeResource(...)` and passes it straight to `getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`. Later it calls `resource.getScopes()`. Neither use is null-checked.

`getResourceTypeResource` returns null in several cases:
- `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false, e.g. the realm's admin permissions were disabled while the admin-permissions client still exists.
- The "Clients" resource does not exist. `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists, so realms initialized before this change never get the new "Clients" resource or the new scopes (configure, map-roles-composite, map-roles-client-scope).

In those cases every client access check by a non-manage-clients admin throws a NullPointerException (500), because the store dereferences `resource.getId()`. The method should return false when the type resource is null.

findings.title: getResourceName not updated for the Clients resource type
findings.body:
`getResourceName` maps only `Users` resources: "All users" for the type resource, or the username for a user. For policies of type `Clients` it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`.

Neither the per-client resources (created with only a name) nor the "Clients" type resource have a display name. Permission representations for client permissions will therefore show null resource names instead of the clientId or an "All clients" label.

Add a `CLIENTS` branch that resolves the client by id and returns its clientId.

findings.title: Removal listener now does no cleanup under V2 (or when FGAP v1 is disabled)
findings.body:
The whole listener is now gated on `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (v1). This was needed because `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws.

As a result, when V2 is enabled, deleting a client leaves behind its per-client resource (named by the client UUID) and any scope permissions referencing it in the admin-permissions resource server. No V2 cleanup was added.

Also, previously the v1 cleanup ran unconditionally. Realms that once used v1 and later disabled the feature will now accumulate orphaned v1 resources and policies for deleted clients, roles and groups.

findings.title: Javadoc for void require* methods says they "Return true"
findings.body:
`requireView()` is documented as "Returns {@code true} if canView() returns true", and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line ~101) as "Returns {@code true} if canViewClientScopes() returns true".

Both methods are `void` and throw ForbiddenException when the check fails. The other `require*` methods in this interface are documented that way. These two docs are wrong.

findings.title: Repeated full policy evaluations per client check
findings.body:
Each `hasPermission(client, scope)` call:
- performs a full policy evaluation over all scopes of the resource, then discards everything but one scope;
- on the fallback path, also runs a `findByResource` query.

`canView(client)` chains `canView()`, then `canConfigure` → `canManage` → `hasPermission(MANAGE)`, then `hasPermission(CONFIGURE)`, then `hasPermission(VIEW)`. That is up to four evaluations of essentially the same resource. `getAccess(client)` repeats this for view, manage and configure.

When listing clients without the view-clients role, this runs for every client in the realm. Evaluate once and check the granted scopes set, or cache per request.

findings.title: New client scopes and override semantics are not actually verified
findings.body:
`testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` grants `CONFIGURE` together with `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE`. The composite-mapping success may therefore come from configure/manage-role checks rather than the new `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` scope.

Other gaps:
- No test covers `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`.
- No test covers `getClientsWithPermission`.
- No test covers a per-client NEGATIVE permission combined with an all-clients permission, as is done for users.

These tests would have exposed the canView short-circuit and the getClientsWithPermission bug.

findings.title: Tests mutate shared realm state without cleanup
findings.body:
Some tests change realm state and never restore it:
- `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates client roles `myclient-role` and `myclient-subRole`, maps one to `myadmin`, and adds a composite. It registers no `realm.cleanup()` actions.
- `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient` and moves a default client scope to optional without reverting.

Other tests in the class index into `getDefaultClientScopes()` and depend on `myclient`'s state. These changes make results order-dependent, and a role-create conflict will occur if the realm is reused.
